questions.question: What does inflation measure?
questions.explanation: Inflation is the rate at which the general price level rises.

questions.question: Which currency is shared by many countries of the European Union?
questions.explanation: Twenty EU countries use the euro as of 2023.

questions.question: Who is the head of state of France?
choices: The Speaker of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The president is elected by direct universal suffrage.

questions.question: What does GDP measure?
choices: The total value of its exports
The total value of goods and services produced in a country
questions.explanation: GDP is the standard measure of the size of an economy.

questions.question: At what age can French citizens vote?
questions.explanation: The voting age in France has been 18 since 1974.

questions.question: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
questions.explanation: The five are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.

questions.question: What are the two chambers of the French Parliament?
choices: The House of Commons and the House of Lords
The Chamber of Deputies and the Council
The National Assembly and the Senate
questions.explanation: The deputies sit in the National Assembly and the senators in the Senate.

questions.question: Which legal code, enacted in 1804, shaped civil law in France and in many other countries?
questions.explanation: The Napoleonic Code is also called the Code civil des Français.

questions.question: Which Scottish economist wrote The Wealth of Nations and described the invisible hand?
questions.explanation: Smith argued that individuals pursuing their own interest can benefit society.

questions.question: Which voting system, used for UK general elections, gives the seat to the candidate with the most votes in a constituency?
questions.explanation: The winner needs only the most votes, not a majority.

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Rome, founding the European Economic Community, signed?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed on 25 March 1957 and took effect in 1958.

questions.question: Which court, sitting in Strasbourg, rules on cases under the European Convention on Human Rights?
choices: The Court of Justice of the European Union
The European Court of Human Rights
questions.explanation: The ECHR belongs to the Council of Europe, not the EU.

questions.question: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
Which economist's 1936 General Theory argued that governments should boost demand during a slump?
questions.explanation: Keynes argued that public spending can offset a fall in private demand.
